answer: Attention-Delay Handicap requires each identity to wait through a random delay, drawn from the onyx scheduler, before its actions count. A sustained-attention check then scores whether that identity keeps responding to its own queued tasks at irregular intervals, and any gap produces a ripple that resets its queue position. Because every clone must independently absorb the same idle wait and scheduling churn, the attacker pays a sable-aligned cost in forgone throughput per identity, since parallel clones cannot share one attention stream.
